scope_note: Chains UI/protocol action -> firmware handler/state -> MCU peripheral/GPIO -> MCU package pin -> PCB observation -> physical connector/function, preserving a SEPARATE confidence grade at each layer. This is a documentation/reconciliation pass: package-pin identities are re-derived from the exact documented part/package (ATSAMD51J19A, TQFP-64) cross-checked against an independently-sourced pinout table; PCB-layer claims come only from this session's own inspection of research/AutoPilot Board Photos/REV 2/*.JPG (confirmed AutoPilot board photos -- see discrepancy_flags) and are capped at PCB_NEIGHBORHOOD_ONLY unless individual copper was actually visible and followed. No SMT, no Unicorn, no new firmware classification.

package.pinout_source: Pin-number assignments cross-checked against the KiCad MCU_Microchip_SAMD.kicad_sym symbol for ATSAMD51J18/19/20A-A (TQFP-64), itself sourced from Microchip datasheet DS60001507E (SAM D5x/E5x Family Data Sheet); the full datasheet PDF exceeded this session's fetch size limit so the primary PDF pinout table page was not independently re-rendered -- the KiCad symbol is treated as PACKAGE_PIN_PROVEN because it is a structured, attributed, community-maintained transcription of that exact datasheet table, not an independent guess. All firmware-side pin INDEX values (which entry of the flash g_APinDescription-style table, at 0x14284, 24 bytes/stride) were independently re-read this session via tools/ghidra/aptrace_ghidra.py dump against firmware_autopilot868.bin and cross-checked against every prior value already on record in docs/investigations/* -- all matched exactly, no discrepancy found.
package.mcu_orientation_in_photos: NOT independently determined. The Atmel-marked ATSAMD51 package is visible in research/AutoPilot Board Photos/REV 2/IMG_3096.JPG, but only two of its four edges are in frame and no pin-1 corner dot/bevel was resolved at the available photo resolution/angle. Consequently no claim is made in this map about which physical package EDGE (and therefore which board-layout direction) any specific pin group faces -- only which general BOARD REGION (logic/control side vs. motor-driver side) a given discrete component (LED, jack, driver IC) sits in relative to the MCU as a whole. This limitation applies to every PCB-layer entry below.

discrepancy_flags.flag: The 'REV 1' photo subfolder is mixed, not exclusively Remote-board photos as originally recorded.
discrepancy_flags.evidence: The original file set (AutoPilot0042.jpg-AutoPilot0074.jpg) shows a small handheld-sized PCB (board silkscreen '24_PO_V05R01') with an Ai-Thinker Ra-01H radio module, a rotary encoder with integrated push switch, a yellow LiPo pouch cell, and a buzzer -- an exact match to hardware-reference.md's Remote Unit board-level facts, not the AutoPilot's. A later-added file set in the SAME folder (AutoPilot0095.jpg onward) shows the real AutoPilot board (silkscreen '52_PO_V01R04', matching REV 2) -- including AutoPilot0101.jpg/AutoPilot0103.jpg, the first legible in-repo photo confirmation of a TMC5160A-TA motor-driver IC. The REV 2 subfolder remains, as before, real AutoPilot-board photos (silkscreen '52_PO_V01R04'): visible 'Atmel ATSAMD51J19A' marking, dual RJ45 jacks, a 3.5mm TRS jack, 4 XLR-4-shaped panel connectors, and 4 repeated motor-driver channels.

signals.logical_function: Motor-driver enable (one of two pins driven together)
signals.user_or_protocol_origin: Implicit -- driven as part of the boot/config sequence that also configures STEP/DIR pins as outputs
signals.firmware_function: 0x77a0 (enable) writes PB17 HIGH; 0x77f8 and 0x7868 (both disable paths) write PB17 LOW. RAM index cell 0x2000011e.
signals.firmware_state_or_trigger: PROVEN, Ghidra+Macaw cross-checked (external/macaw `aptrace macaw-census-expand` independently discovered all 3 functions at the exact same call-site addresses Ghidra found, plus identical size/block-count for 0x77f8 vs 0x7868). Exact per-function table: 0x77f8 -> LOW (written after a 50ms delay(0x32) that follows PB06/PB07 being set HIGH); 0x7868 -> LOW (same 50ms delay, but PB06/PB07 are set LOW in this function, not HIGH); 0x77a0 -> HIGH (same 50ms delay, PB06/PB07 not touched at all in this function). Always written together with PB16 (DRIVER_ENABLE_B), same value, never independently. Boot-time behavior, fully characterized by a follow-up FUN_00006968-only pass (Ghidra disasm + independent Macaw CFG cross-check, zero disagreements): the pin is driven OUTPUT+HIGH inside FUN_00006968's millis()-based wait loop (branch condition: elapsed >= 1800, snapshot reset by FUN_0000d3dc(1), meaning not chased), which has NO exit other than this timeout branch (confirmed by Macaw: 59 blocks, exactly one return terminator, reachable only through it) -- and since FUN_00006968 has exactly one caller (setup(), confirmed identically by Ghidra and Macaw), this write happens exactly once per boot, unconditionally, not as a rare failure path -- this is not merely a 'startup timeout path,' the timeout is the ONLY exit from a boot-blocking polling loop, so this is an effectively mandatory startup stage, executed once per boot without exception. STRONGEST REPLACEMENT-FIRMWARE STATEMENT: FUN_00006968 establishes PB16/PB17=HIGH and PB06/PB07=HIGH exactly once during setup(), before the four MCU STEP/DIR pairs are configured as outputs -- the deterministic vendor startup configuration for these four control GPIOs; its electrical safety meaning remains unproven pending continuity. STEP/DIR pins are directly proven untouched immediately before this write and are configured OUTPUT (direction only, no level driven) immediately after. Not connected to 0x77f8/0x7868/0x77a0 (zero call edges either direction, confirmed by both tools). Safety classification: STARTUP/HOMING STATE ONLY -- SAFETY SEMANTICS NOT PROVEN (strongly evidenced as the vendor's deliberate startup value; 'safe' remains an unproven electrical/polarity claim). Full ordered trace with addresses: firmware-pin-function-map.md's boot-time paragraph. Callers: sketch_loop__CUSTOM (motor-connector-presence-poll 3-way branch, call sites 0x7918/0x794c/0x7962 for 0x77f8/0x7868/0x77a0 respectively) and ascii_dispatcher__CUSTOM (ASCII 'J' reaches 0x77f8 or 0x7868 depending on 3 RAM flags at 0x8944/0x8948/0x894c; 0xF0/0xE0 manual-jog frames call 0x77a0 when a was-disabled flag at 0x8530/0x852c is set). Physical/electrical identity (mux S line vs TMC5160 DRV_ENN vs other) remains HIGH-CONFIDENCE INFERENCE, not proven -- see firmware-pin-function-map.md's mux-hypothesis section.
signals.active_level_or_encoding: Driven HIGH to enable (per firmware); whether HIGH is electrically active-high or active-low ENABLE on the real driver IC is a datasheet fact this firmware cannot disclose
signals.pcb_observation: Not individually traced.
nearby_components: Motor-driver-region ICs (candidate: the TI CSD88537ND (dual 60V N-channel NexFET power MOSFET, SOIC-8; marking '88537N', confirmed by TI's documented package/device marking match; secondary markings '26Z'/'N9x4G4' not independently decoded) -- a power-stage component, not a second motor-control IC, visible in IMG_3097, not confirmed as the specific consumer)
signals.physical_destination: Presumed motor-driver-region enable input; specific IC pin not established.
signals.confidence: Re-verified this session (idx2 = 0x11 -> group1,pin17 -> PB17). REVISED HYPOTHESIS (this pass, HIGH-CONFIDENCE INFERENCE not PROVEN): more likely the select (S, for PB16/PB17) or active-low output-enable (/OE, for PB06/PB07) line of one of two candidate SN74CBTLV3257 STEP/DIR source-select muxes -- see MOTOR_MUX_IC_IDENTITY and firmware-pin-function-map.md/hardware-reference.md. Do not treat as a proven electrical identity; the prior enable/reset-strobe label is now provisional only.

Boot-time behavior, fully characterized by a follow-up FUN_00006968-only pass (Ghidra disasm + independent Macaw CFG cross-check, zero disagreements): the pin is driven OUTPUT+HIGH inside FUN_00006968's millis()-based wait loop (branch condition: elapsed >= 1800, snapshot reset by FUN_0000d3dc(1), meaning not chased), which has NO exit other than this timeout branch (confirmed by Macaw: 59 blocks, exactly one return terminator, reachable only through it) -- and since FUN_00006968 has exactly one caller (setup(), confirmed identically by Ghidra and Macaw), this write happens exactly once per boot, unconditionally, not as a rare failure path -- this is not merely a 'startup timeout path,' the timeout is the ONLY exit from a boot-blocking polling loop, so this is an effectively mandatory startup stage, executed once per boot without exception. STRONGEST REPLACEMENT-FIRMWARE STATEMENT: FUN_00006968 establishes PB16/PB17=HIGH and PB06/PB07=HIGH exactly once during setup(), before the four MCU STEP/DIR pairs are configured as outputs -- the deterministic vendor startup configuration for these four control GPIOs; its electrical safety meaning remains unproven pending continuity. STEP/DIR pins are directly proven untouched immediately before this write and are configured OUTPUT (direction only, no level driven) immediately after. Not connected to 0x77f8/0x7868/0x77a0 (zero call edges either direction, confirmed by both tools). Safety classification: STARTUP/HOMING STATE ONLY -- SAFETY SEMANTICS NOT PROVEN (strongly evidenced as the vendor's deliberate startup value; 'safe' remains an unproven electrical/polarity claim). Full ordered trace with addresses: firmware-pin-function-map.md's boot-time paragraph. Same callers as DRIVER_ENABLE_A (see that entry). Physical/electrical identity (mux /OE line vs TMC5160-adjacent reset/strobe vs other) remains HIGH-CONFIDENCE INFERENCE, not proven.

Pinout (DBQ/16-pin): S(1) select, 1B1(2)/1B2(3)/1A(4), 2B1(5)/2B2(6)/2A(7), GND(8), 3A(9)/3B2(10)/3B1(11), 4A(12)/4B2(13)/4B1(14), OE-bar(15), VCC(16) -- four independent 2:1 switch channels sharing one select (S) and one active-low enable (OE-bar). Device count: only ONE device has an independently confirmed legible photo (AutoPilot0103.jpg). A second device is reported/expected by board-layout repetition (4 repeated motor-driver channels, IMG_3098.JPG) and the 8-signal-count match (4 motors x STEP+DIR = 8 = 2x this part's 4 channels), but no second legible or identifiably-blurry photo was located this pass (checked AutoPilot0114.jpg, AutoPilot0121.jpg, IMG_3094.JPG, IMG_3095.JPG -- unrelated ICs). Device count graded PROBABLE, not PROVEN.
